title: Science Universe — The Discovery Engine
summary: Explore an evolving research ecosystem. Change funding, AI adoption, peer review and replication; intervene in individual laboratories and compare parallel worlds.
description: Science Universe is one interactive, seeded agent-based teaching system for evaluating assumptions about AI-assisted research. Its known-variance Z testing is mathematically grounded; its population, domain priors, research incentives, review probabilities, citation weights, funding and policy mappings are explicitly uncalibrated model choices. Original Lab design rationales and alternatives are inspectable in the Model assumptions decision register. Population and prior sensitivity experiments are available. Independent scientific review is required for empirical claims.

config.learning_goal: Inspect why each simulation rule exists, distinguish theoretically grounded statistical procedures from uncalibrated hypotheses and UI defaults, test robustness to alternative populations and truth priors, and evaluate how AI-assisted throughput interacts with evidence, review and replication. No synthetic outputs are claims about the real scientific system.

sections.title: Observe the ecosystem
sections.hint: Start the world. Each circle is a lab with real simulated agents and research projects.

sections.title: Follow a hypothesis
sections.hint: Select a lab. Watch how hypotheses move from tests to peer review.

sections.title: Change a policy
sections.hint: Open Policies and change research funding, publication pressure or statistical leniency. Change one parameter at a time.

sections.title: Challenge a finding
sections.hint: Select a published claim and request replication. A failed replication does not automatically prove it false.

sections.title: Explore knowledge flows
sections.hint: Switch to Knowledge flow and see how attention and collaboration connect laboratories.

sections.title: Compare two scenarios
sections.hint: Create a comparison from World A. World B begins with identical state, then you can alter its policy and compare the resulting model outcomes.

sections.title: Interpret cautiously
sections.hint: Open Model assumptions. Which conclusions depend on the synthetic rules rather than empirical science?

guidance.hint: You're looking at a synthetic research world, not a forecast. Start the clock and follow one lab.
guidance.concept: Agent-based models explore consequences of explicit rules.

guidance.hint: A new idea entered testing. An interesting hypothesis is not yet evidence.
guidance.concept: Generation and validation are different scientific stages.

guidance.hint: A paper was accepted, but peer review cannot guarantee that its claim is correct.
guidance.concept: Publication and truth are not equivalent.

guidance.hint: Peer review rejected a positive result. The independent check can filter errors but also make mistakes.
guidance.concept: Review is a fallible selection process.

guidance.hint: The result did not replicate. That raises questions; it doesn't alone establish fraud or falsity.
guidance.concept: Power, chance and methods all affect reproducibility.

guidance.hint: An independent test found supporting evidence. One successful repeat still has limits.
guidance.concept: Independent verification provides stronger evidence than self-confirmation.

guidance.hint: This model withdrew a result after failed repeats. Its retraction rule is intentionally simplified.
guidance.concept: Retraction decisions are policy-based and should not be interpreted as a universal scientific rule.

guidance.hint: You changed a model assumption. Let the system run and check downstream consequences.
guidance.concept: Counterfactual comparison needs controlled initial conditions.

guidance.hint: Both worlds share an exact checkpoint. Change one policy in B to explore how outcomes diverge.
guidance.concept: Branching simulations support controlled model counterfactuals.

guidance.hint: One laboratory has more resources. Check whether output, quality and bottlenecks all move together.
guidance.concept: Local resource allocations propagate through connected systems.

guidance.hint: An independent repeat was queued. Its outcome will come from another stochastic test.
guidance.concept: Replication is a test, not an answer supplied by Pulsar.

guidance.hint: You repositioned a lab. Its collaboration links were recomputed in the model.
guidance.concept: Network structure affects how attention spreads.

guidance.hint: The simulation restarted from its seed. Try comparing runs with one altered policy.
guidance.concept: Seeded stochastic simulations can be reproduced if setup and interventions match.
